principle: Every pass line comes from a published threshold, a published benchmark on the same dataset, or a statistical test with a computed sample size. No team-chosen numbers. Metrics without such a source are reported, not judged.

status_values.pass: measured, valid, and meets the evidence-based line
status_values.fail: measured, valid, and does not meet the line
status_values.not_valid: measured, but this data cannot decide (measurement floor above the line, or too few samples for the test)
status_values.not_measured: the input for this item was not given
status_values.report_only: no published pass line exists; the value is reported for tracking only

color.metric: CIEDE2000 between mean Lab of the inner lip, AR render vs real applied photo (hw01_compare.py)

conditions.source: Paravina et al. 2015, J Esthet Restor Dent 27 S1-S9 (doi 10.1111/jerd.12149): 50:50% acceptability threshold dE00 = 1.8; consistent with Lagouvardo et al. 2018, J Prosthodont Res 62(4) 503-508: simulated facial skin on a screen, 90 observers, 50% acceptability dE*ab = 1.81

conditions.rule: AR closer to real than bare in >= 15 of 20 pairs (one-sided sign test p < 0.05)

validity.rule: median skin-ring dE00 between bare and real photo < 1.8, else not_valid
validity.why: skin around the lips is untouched by lipstick; its difference is the photo-to-photo lighting gap that no render can remove

position.metric: dataset-level lip F1 (Dice) = 2*sum(intersection) / (sum(pred)+sum(gt)) over the LaPa test images, upper+lower lip as one region (same aggregation as face-parsing papers)

conditions.source: SegFace, AAAI 2025 (arXiv 2412.08647) Table 1(a): best published LaPa F1 U-lip 88.7-88.8, L-lip 90.5 (448/512 px)

conditions.rule: per-image IoU not significantly lower than the previous version (paired Wilcoxon, one-sided p < 0.05 means fail)

position.caveat: Published models run on a server at 448-512 px and score upper and lower lip separately; VISHUE runs on the phone in real time and scores both lips as one region. The comparison is approximate.

texture.metric: per pair, AR vs bare against the real photo: dL_spread (lower better), dL_hi (lower better), SSIM (higher better)

conditions.rule: AR better than bare in >= 15/20 (one-sided sign test p < 0.05)

texture.pass: all three significant (no multiple-comparison inflation of a pass)
texture.source: exact binomial sign test; SSIM: Wang et al. 2004 IEEE TIP
texture.caveat: dL_spread and dL_hi are VISHUE-designed proxies; their link to perceived gloss is only supported by the small survey so far

naturalness.metric: blind real-vs-AR test on paired photos, AR:real = 1:1

design.why: smallest effect of interest = Cohen's small effect h = 0.20 (accuracy 60% vs 50%); alpha 0.05 two-sided, power 0.80 -> 194 judgments
design.source: Cohen 1988 effect-size conventions; ITU-T P.910 (2026) subjective test design

conditions.rule: upper bound of the 90% CI of accuracy (rater-cluster bootstrap) < 0.60 (equivalence to chance within h = 0.2)
conditions.source: equivalence (TOST) logic; same real-vs-synthetic design as Nightingale & Farid 2022 PNAS (315 people, 48.2%)

conditions.rule: real-minus-AR naturalness score, Cohen's d upper 90% CI bound < 0.2
conditions.source: ITU-T P.910 hidden-reference comparison; Cohen 1988 small effect d = 0.2
